Subject guide

Live technology programs and digital skills training

When a tutorial stops matching your screen, it helps to have someone to ask. Live learning gives you a place to work through the step you missed and understand why it matters.

Explore current programs↗

Start with a task you want to handle

A useful goal might be building your first small program, understanding a data workflow, or getting comfortable with a tool used at work. Name that task before comparing programs. Broad subject labels such as AI or software cover very different levels of depth, so the learning outcomes should do more of the explaining.

Check the setup before the first session

Look for the software, accounts, hardware, and prior knowledge a program requires. A beginner label does not always mean you can arrive without any preparation. If the listing asks for a development environment or a paid tool, work out what you will need before booking. Ask the provider if the requirements are not clear.

Pick a format that matches your question

A workshop can focus on one workflow. A program or boot camp can spread the subject across several sessions. A consultation may suit a specific question you want to discuss with a provider. Read the schedule as carefully as the description so that the time commitment fits your week.

Use the room to understand the process

In an online program, the provider can share a screen and you can ask questions in the session chat. Shared files can keep examples and supporting resources with the program. After a session, the discussion gives enrolled seekers a place to continue a question without losing it in a separate email thread.

Before you choose

A few things to check

  • Tools and account requirements
  • Expected starting knowledge
  • Practice time between sessions
  • The specific skills covered

Current programs, prices, and dates are available in the app.

Choosing your program

Good questions
to ask.

Does every program include software?

Do not assume that software or paid accounts are included. Check the requirements and materials for the program you are considering.

Will a program qualify me for a job?

Learning outcomes describe what a program teaches. They are not a promise of employment or professional certification. Read the details and choose a program for the skills you want to develop.
